purpose: Show how the supported intervention package, real-world conditions and measured adherence connect to outcomes, and where causal claims must stop.
title: Benefits belong to the supported programme as delivered
story: Trials test a dietary pattern delivered with counselling, follow-up and sometimes supplied foods, calorie restriction or physical activity.
Culture, food access, cost, cooking skills and family norms affect whether people can sustain the replacement pattern.
Adherence is measured by self-report and sometimes biomarkers before risk factors, imaging outcomes or clinical events are assessed.
The programme-level evidence does not isolate one ingredient, diet without support or identical effects after adaptation.
observed: PREDIMED supplied extra-virgin olive oil or nuts and provided dietary counselling.
PREDIMED-Plus combined energy restriction, physical activity and intensive behavioural support.
Implementation studies identify cost, access, skills and cultural fit as adherence determinants.
inferred: The arrows show the logic of the evaluated programme, not a quantified mediation model.
The dashed causal boundary marks conclusions that the trial package cannot isolate.
layout_notes: Use one continuous left-to-right programme pathway on a white 3:2 canvas, with a lower context stream feeding into adherence and a dashed causal boundary beneath the outcome stage.
Use lower-case panel letters a, b and c for programme delivered, adherence achieved and outcomes measured; group with alignment and hairlines rather than cards.
Represent foods, counselling and follow-up with restrained scientific-editorial line drawings and local labels; do not use decorative app icons.
Use thin solid arrows for the evaluated sequence and thin dashed arrows for contextual influence; label every arrow.
constraints: Arial throughout; all labels at least 19 px at a 1536 px canvas width.
Keep the title outside the artwork because this is an article figure.
The dashed causal boundary must be prominent enough to prevent single-ingredient or unsupported diet-only conclusions.
Do not imply that biomarkers prove clinical benefit or that every programme includes energy restriction and activity.
Do not imply identical adoption or benefit across cultural settings.
avoid: causal arrows from biomarkers to every disease
exact_text: Benefits belong to the supported programme as delivered
measured by self-report and sometimes biomarkers
The evidence supports the programme as delivered
It does not isolate one ingredient
It does not prove diet without support
It does not guarantee identical effects after adaptation
